literal.prompt: Какой объект скрыт под Восточно-Антарктическим щитом в районе Купола A?

literalGroups.primaryGround: BAS states the Gamburtsev Mountains lie beneath Dome A in East Antarctica (L21); the generic word “object” does not state “mountains” or echo the key name. The four alternatives are distinct Antarctic features; only the BAS-documented subglacial relation fits.

literalGroups.literal: Это горы Гамбурцева. Их рельеф исследуют с помощью радиолокационного зондирования льда.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The AGAP project explored the Gamburtsev Subglacial Mountains and its page lists radio-echo sounding data covering the province.

literalGroups.literal: Подлёдная впадина Бентли — одна из глубочайших точек коренной породы ниже уровня моря.
literalGroups.primaryGround: Bentley is a plausible Antarctic subglacial feature, but BAS identifies its trench as the lowest bed elevation (−2,496 m); it is not the East Antarctic object below Dome A. The note gives its own measurable fact.

literalGroups.literal: Сухие долины Мак-Мердо почти лишены снега и льда: низкая влажность и окружающие горы препятствуют поступлению льда.
literalGroups.primaryGround: McMurdo Dry Valleys are almost devoid of snow and ice; NSF attributes this to low humidity and surrounding mountains blocking nearby glacier ice. The note teaches why this named region is dry.

literalGroups.literal: Происхождение этих гор долго оставалось загадкой для науки.
literalGroups.primaryGround: BAS identifies the Gamburtsev Subglacial Mountains in East Antarctica and says they lie below Dome A; their origin long remained a mystery. This is the unique named object under the stated ice-sheet region, with no answer-name/category cue in the stem.

literalGroups.literal: Купол A — высшая область Антарктического ледникового щита во внутренней Восточной Антарктиде.
literalGroups.primaryGround: Dome A is the highest, perhaps coldest, place on the East Antarctic Ice Sheet; the note accurately identifies the surface feature rather than the buried object.
